newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey's Yilmaz says minority govt to be approved.
newsitem.headline: Turkey's Yilmaz says minority govt to be approved.

text.p: Turkey's prime minister-designate Mesut Yilmaz said on Thursday the president had vowed to approve a planned secularist coalition that would keep the Islamists out of power, despite its current lack of a majority.

"The president told me he would approve a government with the support of four parties," Yilmaz told a news conference in reference to four opposition parties, currently short of a majority in the 550-seat parliament.
Secularist Yilmaz has said he would present a government list at the start of next week to President Suleyman Demirel, who has to approve the bid before it goes to parliament for a confidence vote.
Main opposition leader Yilmaz is relying on defections from the rival conservative True Path Party of Tansu Ciller to win such a vote.
A True Path MP said on Thursday she had quit Tansu Ciller's True Path, boosting Yilmaz's efforts. She was the third MP to abandon Ciller since rival Yilmaz was asked to form a government last Friday.
Turkey's first Islamist leader Necmettin Erbakan resigned as prime minister last week under pressure from the secularist military.
